info.description:
Face authentication as an API. Enroll a subject once, verify them in under a
second, and get an audit trail for every decision.

**Two authentication surfaces:**

* `/v1/*` — the public API, authenticated with an API key (`Authorization: Bearer fvas_live_…`)
* `/v1/console/*` — the dashboard API, authenticated with a JWT

A failed *verification* is a `200` with `"decision": "rejected"` — that is a
successful answer to the question asked. Only a failed *request* is an error.
info.title: Fvas

post.description:
**The secret is returned once and never again.** Only its SHA-256 digest is stored, so there is nothing to retrieve later - if it is lost, rotate the key.

Requires a verified email address: a key we cannot reach the owner of is a key nobody can be told to revoke.

delete.description: Effective on the next request. No cache, no grace period.

post.description:
Issues a replacement and keeps the old key working for **24 hours**, so you can redeploy without a window of 401s. After that the old key stops working on its own.

Use `DELETE` instead when a key is known to be compromised - that takes effect on the next request, with no overlap.
Always returns the same response whether or not the address is registered. Varying the status, message, or timing would make this an account-enumeration oracle.
Returns a short-lived access token and a rotating refresh token. The refresh token is intended for an httpOnly cookie set by the BFF, never for browser storage.
Revokes the current token family, or every session for the user.

post.description:
Runs detect, quality gating, embedding and duplicate detection, then creates a profile. Re-enrolling supersedes the previous profile and increments its version.

Per-image results are returned on success as well as failure, so a capture UI can tell the user *which* frame was weak.

**409 `duplicate_face_detected`** means the face already belongs to another subject. That is a decision to surface, not an error to retry.

post.description:
The core endpoint.

**A rejected verification is a `200`.** `decision` carries the outcome; only a failed *request* is a `4xx`.

`inconclusive` is never collapsed into `rejected` - telling someone they are not who they claim when the truth is that the room is too dark would be both wrong and would corrupt your fraud metrics with lighting problems.

Send `Idempotency-Key` on retries: the first response is replayed for 24 hours without re-running the pipeline or charging quota a second time.

429.description: Rate limit or monthly quota exhausted; carries `Retry-After`

post.description:
The signing secret is returned **once**. Verify every delivery with it:

`Fvas-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>` is HMAC-SHA256 over `{t}.{raw body}`. Reject anything more than five minutes old, and compare in constant time.

Delivery is at-least-once - dedupe on `Fvas-Event-Id`.
